checks.message: event ids, explanation ids, prediction ids and behavioral test names are unique, and all 3 behavioral test(s) and 3 prediction(s) reference two different existing events

no approximate dates: none of the 10 event quote(s) across 5 event(s) — nor any FULL source sentence/heading unit containing one — states a decade form ("1770s") or attaches an approximation qualifier ("circa", "c.", "ca.", "approx.", "around", "about", "roughly", "sometime in", "early/mid/late" — including article and day-first forms like "around the 4th of July 1776") to a date expression

all 5 event date(s) are stated by ONE COMPLETE connected date expression of the SOURCE in a CLEAN context (round-3 allow-list: no qualifier, temporal bound, unconsumed era token, century wording, alternative, range connector + number, '?' or markup within two words) lying inside ONE sentence unit of a counted verbatim quote's located source span: the year (directly, or from a clean source title stating exactly one plain year when one expression states the month and day), plus the month and day where stated
all 5 event (year, month, day) tuples are distinct
all 3 behavioral test(s) and 3 prediction(s) recomputed from the event dates: earlierEventId is strictly earlier than laterEventId at the precision both events state
all references resolve: 1 spec source(s), 1 cited sourceId(s)
sha256 verified for 1 source(s): stored hash and recomputed text hash both match the spec

all 15 evidence quote(s) count as evidence (>= 8 normalised characters with >= 3 letters/digits, or a compact "=" equation with >= 3) and all 15 resolvable quote(s) appear in their source text after whitespace normalisation; every explanation and every event has >= 1 counted quote

no generated display field (title, objectives, explanations, prediction prompts, behavioral test names, event labels, scenario labels) mentions the publisher or uses attribution/endorsement wording naming a source or authority; evidence quotes are exempt
Explanation prose is AI-generated; quotes, numbers and ranges are machine-checked, the wording needs teacher review.

repair weakened the spec: event "e2" changed (evidence quotes changed) even though its date check passed on the baseline (an event that passed keeps its id, label, date and quotes unless a date-class finding names it) (a timeline repair must fix the failing checks without changing the engine, adding events, dropping the event count below 5, removing or rewriting an event that passed its date checks on the baseline, or changing a case pair that was strictly ordered on the baseline; only an item that failed the recomputed baseline checks, or the exact fields where a finding's affected paths intersect the recomputed baseline failures, may change)
